research_question: Can a cross-market rotation transfer be defined as a later recipient event rather than a rank-one source event, preserving the V15 W13 transfer winner while removing the remaining V15 W20 loss?

hypothesis.unchanged_v15_execution: FAR retains the V15 post-only causal displacement retrace, sweep-based structural stop and external-liquidity target; confirmation-close market chasing and internal void stops remain disabled.
hypothesis.source_transfer_boundary: SEMANTIC_FAR_ROTATION_TRANSFER_EVENT_DISPLACEMENT is executable only when event_direction_rank is greater than one. Rank-one candidates are the source of the move, not recipients of transfer, and become UNRESOLVED.
hypothesis.unchanged_roles: All other FAR and AAC roles, thresholds, risk sizing, costs, global arbitration and NautilusTrader order handling are unchanged.
hypothesis.development_only: W13 and W20 are already exposed. They can reject the mechanism or select the frozen policy for untouched validation, but cannot support a success claim.

selection.method: Two exposed weeks isolate the only two V15 rotation-displacement plans: W13 rank-three winner and W20 rank-one loss.

claim_rules: W13 and W20 are exposed development periods and cannot support a success claim.
The only new rule is event order: a rotation-transfer recipient cannot be event rank one.
Passing advances the unchanged V16 policy to the full exposed regression and then a source-frozen untouched continuous account.
